title: app-manifest.json
$comment: HeyHi Confidential. Emitted by the app-recon skill (Sheerline Lane C). Field list is binding per plans/plan-sheerline-fdde-loop-2026-09-07.md 3.3; versioned 1.0, additive thereafter. Consumed by app-to-figma (Lane B), the intent skills (Lane D), and feature-increment (Lane F). Every copy row and every components_used row carries file:line provenance; every claim the read could not ground lives in unverified[]. Cross-field rules the schema cannot express (an endpoint named without a spec must appear in unverified[]; a shown fact must trace to a file) are enforced in SKILL.md Step 5, not here.

system_id.description: A non-identifying label for the application under recon (never a client name; the hermetic seal holds). The worked example uses the repo's own directory name.

source_commit.description: The exact commit the recon read. In delta mode this is the new HEAD; the baseline it was diffed against is recorded in the brief, not here.

tier.description: The recon tier the read ran at (the off-ramp). 0 skip, 1 light, 2 full. The precedence rule forces 2 for any change that writes data, changes auth or entitlement, or crosses an architecture boundary; when it does not fire, the tier is a human call (an empty slot, recorded in the brief).

surfaces.description: One row per surface the read covers: a surface it fanned out, or a candidate it found in the router but did not fan out this pass. A surface is a product feature-area with its own container directory (a route and its container), not a file. Which of these surfaces are finally in scope for the artifact is the human's call (an empty slot); the read lists the candidates, the human selects.

route.description: The URL route or path the surface renders at, verified from the router wiring.

container_dir.description: The container directory that owns the surface (the fan-out unit).

breakpoints.description: Breakpoints the surface is built against, read from the layout wiring; empty when none are declared.

theme.description: The surface's theme, confirmed from the theme wiring, not inferred from surrounding chrome. Unresolved themes go to unverified[].

architecture_target.description: Which architecture the surface targets (e.g. current app vs a migration target), read from the auth and shell wiring. Unresolved targets go to unverified[].

components_used.description: Components the surface renders, with the props actually passed and their defaults. Every row carries source provenance (file:line).

items.$comment: All four plan-3.3 fields are required keys. props_passed and defaults are objects that may be empty ({} = no props passed / no declared defaults), but the key may not be omitted: a component whose call site could not be read to determine its props is an unverified[] row, not a components_used row with the props silently dropped.

props_passed.description: The props actually passed at the call site (not the full prop surface); {} when none are passed.

defaults.description: Defaults declared by the component for props not passed; {} when none are declared.

source.description: Provenance: the import path or package the component resolves to, with the file:line of the call site. Required on every row (the read never names a component without a source).

copy.description: Real copy strings the surface renders, each with file:line provenance. Never copy remembered or invented text.

text.description: The literal string as it appears in the source.

role.description: The copy's role (heading, body, label, cta, and so on).

file.description: The file the string lives in. Required on every row.

line.description: The line the string lives on. Required on every row.

endpoints.description: The endpoints this surface calls, as pointers (method, path, and the hook that calls them). The full verified endpoint registry with OpenAPI pointers is the top-level endpoints[]; these are the per-surface call sites.

hook.description: The hook or call site that issues the request.

in_flight.description: When a surface is mid-migration, the branch it changes on and where the end state lands, so a downstream spec targets the destination, not soon-dead code. Read-only branch scan; never a checkout.

endpoints.description: The verified endpoint registry. Each endpoint carries JSON pointers into the OpenAPI spec, verified against the schema and the handlers (Tier 2 only). An endpoint that cannot be grounded against a spec is not listed here; it goes to unverified[]. Empty for an application with no API (an honest empty array, not an omission).

items.$comment: All six fields are required per plan 3.3 so a partially-read endpoint cannot pass as complete; request_pointer and response_pointer are nullable (null = the spec is silent), so a grounded endpoint with no request/response body still validates, while an endpoint row that OMITS a pointer fails (the read must state 'no pointer' explicitly, never leave it ambiguous).

request_pointer.description: JSON pointer into the OpenAPI spec for the request shape, or null when the spec has none. Required key; the value may be null but the key may not be omitted.

response_pointer.description: JSON pointer into the OpenAPI spec for the response shape, or null when the spec has none. Required key; the value may be null but the key may not be omitted.

auth.description: The auth the endpoint requires, verified from the handler ("none" for an unauthenticated endpoint).

entitlement.description: The entitlement or role gate the endpoint enforces, verified from the handler ("none" when ungated).

capabilities.description: What the application can do, verified from wiring. An honest empty case (no auth, no writes) is recorded as such, never omitted.

auth_model.description: The auth model, or "none" for an unauthenticated surface.

roles.description: Roles the application distinguishes; empty when none.

writes.description: The write paths the application exposes; empty for a read-only or static application.

offline_sync.description: Whether the application has an offline or sync capability, and its shape; false or "none" when it does not.

feature_flags.description: Feature flags that gate surfaces or capabilities; empty when none.

unverified.description: Every claim the read could not ground, by surface. An unmounted repo, an endpoint with no spec, an unresolved theme or architecture target: each is a row here, never a guess elsewhere in the manifest. This array being present (empty with a one-line reason, or populated) is a completeness signal, not a failure. Resolving each item is the human's call (an empty slot).

surface.description: The surface (or "global") the ungrounded claim belongs to.

reason.description: Why it could not be grounded (repo not mounted, no OpenAPI spec, wiring unresolved).
